docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A scarce rail franchise with a measurable operating problem
Source: compiled from: https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/Annual-Report/2010/cp-ar-2010.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311068899/o72585e6vk.htm
Date: 2011-07-27

Canadian Pacific operates a transcontinental freight railway in Canada and the United States. It sells transportation rather than the commodities transported. Its physical right-of-way, terminals and connections form the competitive asset; replicating a network requires land, construction, regulatory approvals and sufficient traffic density. These barriers do not make traffic or profits immune to a recession. Grain, fertilizer, coal, industrial production and consumer imports all affect demand. The 2010 annual report is the source for the following full-year figures, in Canadian dollars.

| FY2010 revenue stream | C$ millions |
|---|---:|
| Intermodal | 1,347.9 |
| Grain | 1,135.7 |
| Industrial and consumer products | 902.8 |
| Coal | 490.8 |
| Sulphur and fertilizers | 474.8 |
| Automotive | 316.4 |
| Forest products | 184.9 |
| Other | 128.2 |
| Total | 4,981.5 |

There was no customer exceeding 10% of revenue in 2010 or 2009. Intermodal serves domestic container movements and international port traffic; bulk commodities provide different demand exposures. Fuel recoveries help offset diesel costs but introduce timing and mix effects. Higher reported revenue can therefore reflect fuel rather than better underlying pricing.

In 2010 CP moved 2,660.6 thousand carloads and 126,428 million revenue ton-miles. Freight revenue per carload was C$1,824; intermodal yielded C$1,260 per carload and sulphur/fertilizers C$2,679. These are revenue measures, not contribution margins: distance, weight, train configuration and equipment needs differ. Segment-level operating profits are not supplied here.

Fred Green is president and CEO. The operating ratio, expenses divided by revenue, is the primary efficiency yardstick: 77.6% in 2010. Its complement, 22.4%, is operating margin, not return on capital. An improvement can come from pricing, train productivity, utilization or traffic recovery; cutting essential maintenance would not create equivalent sustainable value.

At June 30, 2011, 169.4 million common shares were outstanding; Q2 diluted weighted-average shares were 170.7 million. The company has public shareholders rather than a disclosed controlling owner in this source set. Net property of C$11,981.2 million emphasizes that this is an asset-intensive network, not a capital-light royalty. Management's explanations and operating targets should be tested against peers rather than treated as proof of an inevitable turnaround.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three reported fiscal years and the first half of 2011
Source: compiled from: https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/Annual-Report/2010/cp-ar-2010.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311068899/o72585e6vk.htm
Date: 2011-07-27

All monetary amounts below are C$ millions, except per-share figures. Annual results come from the 2010 annual report, with its restated comparative figures; interim results were released July 27, 2011. The annual table uses reported consolidation rather than silently adding a full year of Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern to 2008.

| Metric | FY2008 | FY2009 | FY2010 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reported revenue | 5,048.5 | 4,402.2 | 4,981.5 |
| Reported operating income | 1,039.0 | 830.1 | 1,116.1 |
| Reported operating ratio | 79.4% | 81.1% | 77.6% |
| Net income | 627.8 | 550.0 | 650.7 |
| Diluted EPS | 4.04 | 3.30 | 3.85 |
| Adjusted diluted EPS | 4.06 | 2.51 | 3.87 |
| Declared dividend/share | 0.9900 | 0.9900 | 1.0575 |

Revenue recovered 13.2% in 2010, calculated from the reported totals. For like-for-like 2008 comparison, the annual report separately supplies pro-forma revenue of C$5,349.2 million including DM&E throughout the year. Using that denominator changes the apparent 2009 contraction. Adjusted 2009 operating ratio was 81.7%, versus reported 81.1%; property gains and a shortline lease termination affected comparability.

| Interim metric | Q2 2010 | Q2 2011 | H1 2011 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,234.2 | 1,264.5 | 2,427.9 |
| Operating income | 274.1 | 230.5 | 339.7 |
| Net income | 166.6 | 128.0 | 161.7 |
| Diluted EPS | 0.98 | 0.75 | 0.95 |
| Cash from operations | 187.1 | 212.3 | 347.3 |
| Property additions | 168.0 | 218.4 | 351.6 |

H1 operating cash less property additions was negative C$4.3 million, calculated, before C$91.4 million of cash dividends. This conventional cash-flow subtraction differs from CP's defined “free cash,” which also considers investing flows, dividends and specified adjustments. Q2 conventional free cash flow alone was negative C$6.1 million. Neither figure should be annualized through a seasonal railway.

June 30 cash was C$267.8 million; current debt C$278.8 million and long-term debt C$3,918.8 million. Calculated gross debt is C$4,197.6 million and debt less cash C$3,929.8 million, excluding pension liabilities of C$1,019.9 million. Annual CFO/capex series, buyback totals and a verified issuer ROIC series are not available in this extracted snapshot; EPS is not a substitute for them.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: Flood disruption, higher fuel costs and management's recovery claim
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311068899/o72585e6vk.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311037682/o70312e6vk.htm
Date: 2011-07-27

The latest available quarterly release is Q2 2011, published July 27. Revenue was C$1,264.5 million, up C$30.3 million; operating expenses were C$1,034.0 million, up C$73.9 million. Operating income declined to C$230.5 million from C$274.1 million. Net income was C$128.0 million and diluted EPS C$0.75, versus C$166.6 million and C$0.98. The operating ratio deteriorated to 81.8% from 77.8%; the first-half ratio was 86.0%, versus 80.0%.

Fred Green said: “We had almost 90 separate outages during the quarter and our engineering team worked as swiftly as possible to bring the track back.” Management rerouted and detoured traffic over other railways and incurred higher operating costs to deliver customers' freight. Green's assessment was: “Repairs are now complete and service levels are returning to normal.” This is a management statement about conditions in July, not independently verified evidence of a sustained earnings recovery.

Average fuel price increased 37% to US$3.50 per gallon. Fuel expense rose from C$177.9 million to C$237.4 million, while compensation and benefits fell from C$349.7 million to C$336.1 million. Purchased services and other expenses increased from C$203.3 million to C$227.3 million. These line items suggest that the problem cannot be reduced to excessive headcount alone.

The April 21 first-quarter release provides the immediately preceding guidance context. Q1 EPS was C$0.20 and operating income C$109.2 million, against C$0.60 and C$206.6 million a year earlier. Green said: “We remain committed to delivering our two- to four-year target of a low 70’s operating ratio and providing a quality service offering.” The target is management's, with a multi-year timeframe, not a promise for the next quarter.

The practical underwriting question is how much of the gap reflects temporary outages and how much reflects persistent operating design. A low-70s ratio implies a much stronger margin than the latest 81.8%, but reaching it requires service recovery, adequate capacity and cost discipline simultaneously. Neither a more aggressive external target nor a committed replacement executive is established by these releases. No third-quarter results are in the information set.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: September 23 market observations and reproducible valuation arithmetic
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CP.TO?period1=1285113600&period2=1316822400&interval=1d; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CP?period1=1285113600&period2=1316822400&interval=1d; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311068899/o72585e6vk.htm; http://blog.yardeni.com/2011/09/s-500-valuation.html
Date: 2011-09-23

Historical daily observations are restricted to September 23, 2011 and earlier. Yahoo's split-adjusted close/OHLC and volume series are converted to contemporaneous CP share units using a factor of five for price and its reciprocal for volume. These are reconstructed historical observations, not a live quote or a claim about a subsequent investment's acquisition cost. Canadian and US listings must not be mixed when calculating earnings multiples.

| Observation | Value |
|---|---:|
| September 23 Toronto close | C$48.59 |
| September 23 New York close | US$47.24 |
| Toronto high in preceding approximately 52 weeks | C$69.48 |
| Toronto low in same window | C$46.01 |
| Toronto close versus window high | −30.1%, calculated |
| Toronto September 23 share volume | 986,100 |
| Toronto mean daily volume, last 20 observations | 674,735 |

Using the last disclosed 169.4 million outstanding shares, the Toronto close implies approximately C$8.23 billion equity capitalization. Adding June 30 debt less cash of C$3.930 billion yields approximately C$12.16 billion enterprise value, excluding pension adjustments and changes since June. These are analyst calculations with deliberately mixed market and balance-sheet observation dates identified.

FY2010 EPS of C$3.85 gives a 12.6x historical fiscal-year P/E. A trailing-twelve-month approximation replaces H1 2010 EPS of C$1.58 with H1 2011 EPS of C$0.95: C$3.22, implying 15.1x. Summing period EPS is approximate because diluted share counts vary. This is not a forward multiple. An authenticated September consensus EPS estimate and the company's five-to-ten-year multiple range are not available in this source set. No forward P/E or consensus growth figure is invented.

For context, Ed Yardeni's September 20 note describes S&P 500 forward P/E as 11.3x. That forward market measure is not directly comparable to CP's depressed trailing earnings.

A separate Yahoo historical Toronto close comparison from September 22, 2006 to September 23, 2011 gives CP price return of −8.0% versus Canadian National's +45.7%, calculated from like-date series. Dividends are excluded. Source queries use period1=1158883200 and the same period2 for CP.TO and CNR.TO. The comparison measures sustained relative underperformance, not the cause or certainty of reversal.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Weather excuse or structurally inferior execution?
Source: compiled from: https://financialpost.com/investing/flooding-hits-cp-profit; https://www.joc.com/article/flood-woes-cut-canadian-pacific-profit-23-percent-5239574; https://financialpost.com/investing/trading-desk/time-to-buy-cp-rail-rbc; https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/Annual-Report/2010/cp-ar-2010.pdf
Date: 2011-07-28

Eric Lam in the Financial Post on July 27 reported a 23% decline in CP quarterly profit. His report put the revenue increase at 2% and expense increase at 7%, with fuel prices rising 37%. Bloomberg-surveyed analysts had expected approximately C$0.72 EPS on C$1.26 billion revenue; actual diluted EPS was C$0.75. The quarter was poor, but it was not an earnings miss against that particular survey. Confusing an absolute deterioration with an unexpected miss would overstate the dislocation.

The Journal of Commerce's John D. Boyd, July 27, described revenue growth of just 2.5% as behind other major carriers. The concern is relative performance: if the industry enjoys pricing and recovering volumes while CP struggles with service, the gap may reflect management or network economics rather than a generalized rail recession.

An opposing contemporaneous interpretation is available. Jonathan Ratner's July 28 Financial Post account says RBC analyst Walter Spracklin upgraded CP from Outperform to Top Pick. Spracklin wrote: “A key component of our positive thesis is the view that the weather-related effects are now behind the company and operations are reverting to normal.” The article reports C$16 million of weather-related cost effects, rising gross ton-miles and car miles per day, and potential recovery of deferred bulk volumes in the second half.

Spracklin's valuation interpretation was: “In our view, investors are getting a free call option on operating targets that, when compared to the rest of the group, are modest at best.” The article reports C$13 per share upside if operating targets are met and calls CP the cheapest rail in the group. These are an analyst's conditional estimates, not an established asset value or a precise September peer-multiple table.

The annual report identifies genuine recurring exposures: freight demand, rates, fuel prices, exchange rates, labor disputes, pensions and maintenance costs. Geography and commodity mix can affect ratios even with equally competent management. An investment needs evidence that service and utilization can improve without sacrificing safety or necessary capex. A ratio gap alone neither proves fraud nor establishes that peer economics are fully transferable to CP's network.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Class I benchmarks and the public record of an experienced operator
Source: compiled from: https://www.smart-union.org/railroads-2010-how-sweet-it-was/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000119312511010650/dex991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000027794811000005/qfr_q42010.htm; https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/newsroom/news-archive/2011/norfolk-southern-reports-2010-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16868/000001686811000027/form6k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16868/000095010302001378/dec1302_6k.htm
Date: 2011-07-25

The table compares fiscal 2010 ratios available by January 2011. Margin is calculated as 100% less operating ratio. SMART's January 28 rail-industry roundup supplies the Canadian National figure; the other US figures are corroborated by the cited issuer releases.

| Railway | FY2010 operating ratio | Implied operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|
| Canadian Pacific | 77.6% | 22.4% |
| Canadian National | 63.6% | 36.4% |
| Union Pacific | 70.6% | 29.4% |
| CSX | 71.1% | 28.9% |
| Norfolk Southern | 71.9% | 28.1% |

The latest same-quarter Canadian comparison is starker: CP's Q2 2011 ratio was 81.8%, while CN reported 61.3% on July 25. CN revenue increased 8% to C$2,260 million; operating income increased 8% to C$874 million. CN said its own network encountered floods, forest fires and mudslides. Differences in where disruptions occur matter, but adverse weather was not unique to CP.

CN reiterated expected adjusted EPS growth of up to 15% for 2011 from its C$4.20 base and approximately C$1.2 billion free cash flow, as defined by CN. It planned C$1.7 billion capex, including more than C$1 billion for track infrastructure. Superior operating ratios do not eliminate rail reinvestment.

Union Pacific's January 20 release reported 2010 revenue carload growth across all six business groups, 10.8% ROIC, C$-independent US$5.53 EPS, and nearly US$1.25 billion share repurchases. Norfolk Southern reported revenue growth of 19% and EPS growth of 45%; CSX reported operating income growth of 35%. Peer growth underscores the opportunity cost of persistent operational underperformance.

Hunter Harrison has a public operating background, independently of any proposed role at CP. CN's December 13, 2002 release named him CEO effective January 1, 2003; he had been CEO of Illinois Central from 1993 to 1998 and CN COO from March 1998. CN's November 15, 2005 SEC-filed presentation describes an operating-ratio progression into the mid-60s: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16868/000095010305002331/nov0405_6k.htm. This establishes relevant experience, not his willingness or contractual ability to take another job. Comparable dated peer market multiples are unavailable here; operating ratios are the reliable benchmark.
docs.D07_recent_event_timeline.md:
Title: Operating recovery promises and a rail-activism precedent
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166893/000095012311005522/o68062ae6vk.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311037682/o70312e6vk.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16875/000095012311068899/o72585e6vk.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000095015708000543/form8-k.htm
Date: 2011-07-27

**January 26, 2011 — prior-year results.** CP announced 2010 results. Fourth-quarter revenue increased 13% across all business lines. The annual operating ratio of 77.6% represented a recovery from the recession year. The existence of that recovery matters: a turnaround case must explain why the gap remains attractive after some improvement has already occurred.

**April 21, 2011 — winter-related setback.** First-quarter EPS fell to C$0.20 from C$0.60, with almost flat revenue and C$94.0 million more operating expense. Green described severe winter outages constraining both capacity and customer service. He reaffirmed a low-70s operating-ratio target over two to four years. That is a publicly stated performance yardstick against which shareholders can evaluate execution.

**July 25, 2011 — CN's comparison.** Canadian National reported 61.3% operating ratio, 8% revenue growth and 12% adjusted EPS growth for Q2. CN retained its annual outlook despite uncertainty about global growth. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16868/000001686811000027/form6k.htm. The release supplies current peer evidence rather than requiring an analyst to extrapolate an old cycle's peak.

**July 27, 2011 — flood impact.** CP's Q2 release reported C$0.75 EPS, an 81.8% ratio and almost 90 outages. Management said repairs were complete. Whether this is an inflection or another temporary explanation is still unresolved. No realized third-quarter recovery is assumed.

**Governance precedent, July 2008 — CSX.** This is older contextual evidence, not a new CP event. CSX's July 29, 2008 filing documents board entry for TCI/3G nominees Alexandre Behring and Gilbert Lamphere and director John McPherson following incumbent resignations. The filing explicitly preserves TCI/3G nominees' rights concerning the contested election. It demonstrates that shareholder intervention in a large railroad can reach board composition; it does not prove intervention improves operations or that identical tactics fit Canadian law.

No announcement in this source set establishes a CP CEO change, agreed succession candidate or committed activist transaction by the cutoff. The investable question is whether a shareholder can identify specific operational changes, retain a qualified operator and obtain board support. Public operating targets are a starting point, not an executable governance plan.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: Concentrated activist capital, existing exposures and available principles
Source: compiled from: https://www.barrons.com/articles/SB50001424052970203425804576321430205901612; https://www.cnbc.com/2011/09/14/ackman-to-reveal-investment-at-delivering-alpha.html; https://www.marketfolly.com/2011/08/why-bill-ackman-bought-more-citigroup-c.html; https://nypost.com/2011/06/17/ackman-pumps-up/
Date: 2011-09-14

Barron's Jonathan Laing, May 23, 2011, put Pershing Square funds under management at US$10.3 billion, versus US$6.7 billion in August 2008. This is the latest authenticated firmwide AUM figure in this source set; it is not September's exact NAV or a measure of immediately available cash. A concentrated new investment must be assessed against substantial existing exposures.

CNBC's Margaret Popper, September 14, reports the June 30 disclosed equity portfolio at US$6.4 billion, with five positions approximately 84% of value:

| Holding | Approximate weight of disclosed portfolio |
|---|---:|
| J.C. Penney | 21% |
| General Growth Properties | 19% |
| Fortune Brands | 17% |
| Citigroup | 15% |
| Kraft | 12% |

These are rounded 13F-style portfolio weights reported by CNBC, not percentages of firm NAV. They omit cash, shorts, many derivatives and non-reportable securities. No audited cash balance is available. Market Folly's August 30 account of the investor letter says Ackman deployed US$600 million during recent volatility; the source does not establish how much uncommitted capital remains.

The publicly expressed approach is concentration, intrinsic-value analysis and action to improve businesses. The New York Post, June 17, reproduces this May 25 investor-letter statement: “We believe that these larger businesses generally offer greater opportunities for the kinds of corporate change that we often pursue.” The point is an opportunity to influence an enterprise, not merely to trade a price rebound.

Market Folly quotes his contemporary Citigroup analysis: “Based on this disclosure, we believe that Citi is adequately capitalized to withstand the losses that may result from adverse outcomes from the Greek and other Eurozone debt crises.” That reasoning explicitly considers an adverse scenario rather than only expected earnings. It is sector context, not a statement about CP.

CNBC's profile describes earlier McDonald's restructuring proposals, General Growth real-estate involvement and costly Target/Borders experiences. Those examples show both willingness to pursue governance change and the danger of treating asset value as sufficient protection. There is no authenticated pre-cutoff Ackman statement specifically endorsing CP in this source set; none is supplied as a fabricated quotation. Exact recent exits and a full cash reconciliation remain unavailable.

drivers.driver: Close a large operating-efficiency gap in a durable rail franchise rather than underwrite an inferior franchise.
Recruit Hunter Harrison, whose prior operating record makes the management-change case concrete.
Use board change to enable an operational plan focused on service, utilization and costs.
Translate improved operating performance into materially higher per-share earnings.
drivers.quote: At the inception of our investment in 2011, CP earned $3.15 per share.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight documents. Strong primary quarterly operating data and four-peer ratio table. Exact September forward EPS, peer multiples, historical multiple range, full annual cash-flow series and original Ackman entry quotations not recovered. Driver quotations not invented: three drivers are attributed paraphrases using explicitly later sources, confined to this answer key. Latest portfolio weights are contemporary CNBC reporting of June 13F, not direct 13F extraction. Historical Yahoo observations reconstructed in original share units; valuation and returns explicitly calculated. No future operator appointment, campaign target or stake disclosure in docs.

valuation.eps_path: Growth driven by 800-1000 bps operating ratio improvement to low 70s
valuation.downside_case: Stock remains a value trap with limited multiple expansion if self-help fails

drivers.driver: The company operates a scarce, transcontinental freight rail network protected by significant barriers to entry [D01].
A substantial operational self-help opportunity exists, as the current 81.8% operating ratio lags industry peers like Canadian National at 63.6% [D03, D06].
The market views operational failures as structural, whereas we identify them as fixable execution and management issues [D03, D06].
We can acquire this high-moat asset at an attractive entry valuation of ~15x trailing earnings while management targets a significant margin expansion [D03, D04, D06].

kill_criteria: Operating ratio fails to show sequential improvement toward the low 70s target over two consecutive quarters.
Management demonstrates a persistent inability to mitigate the impact of weather-related outages on service consistency.
Revenue growth turns negative for two quarters due to a secular decline in core commodity volumes that overrides self-help margin gains.
The board rejects a collaborative engagement regarding operational and management improvements.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the service and margin gap relative to Canadian National is structural and inherent to the network's design rather than a result of poor management and execution.
final.memo:
We are initiating a position in the Company because it operates a scarce, transcontinental freight rail network that serves as critical infrastructure for the North American economy [D01]. Despite the high quality of the underlying asset, the company suffers from chronic operational underperformance, with an operating ratio of 81.8% that lags best-in-class peers by nearly 2,000 basis points [D03, D06].

The market has mispriced this security by assuming these persistent service gaps and margin issues are structural failures [D03]. We believe the gap is fundamentally a management and execution issue [D03, D06]. By closing the performance gap toward the company's own stated 'low 70s' operating ratio target, there is significant room for earnings growth regardless of the broader macro environment [D03].

We are acquiring our stake at a 15.1x trailing multiple, which is attractive for a dominant, high-barrier-to-entry franchise [D04]. As management executes on the necessary operational improvements, we expect a substantial increase in earnings per share, providing an expected IRR of approximately 22% in our base case [D03, D04].

We intend to act as an active owner, engaging with the Board to accelerate the implementation of an operational review and a rigorous, time-bound plan to reach benchmark-level efficiency [D03, D06]. Our goal is to ensure the company achieves its potential as a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative rail operator [D01, D03].

valuation.eps_path: Expansion to low 70s operating ratio yielding C$6.50-C$7.00 EPS
valuation.downside_case: Asset value provides a floor; failure to improve operations leaves the stock as a low-multiple value trap.

drivers.driver: Canadian Pacific operates a critical, high-barrier-to-entry transcontinental network of right-of-way and terminals [D01].
The company suffers from a massive operational inefficiency, with a Q2 2011 operating ratio of 81.8% compared to 61.3% for its best-in-class peer [D06].
The efficiency gap is not structural but execution-based, fixable through the implementation of precision railroading [D03, D06].
New leadership and management discipline can drive an earnings transformation, moving the operating ratio to the low 70s and unlocking significant intrinsic value [D03, D06, D07].

kill_criteria: Management fails to implement precision railroading or rejects a path to operating ratio improvement.
Operating ratio remains stagnant or worsens over four consecutive quarters despite management changes.
Regulatory or legislative bodies prohibit the necessary operational restructuring or network changes required for margin expansion.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the operating ratio disparity relative to peers is fundamentally linked to the physical constraints of the network rather than poor management execution.
final.memo:
Canadian Pacific is a critical North American infrastructure asset, providing essential transcontinental freight services across a high-barrier-to-entry network [D01]. Despite the quality of this monopoly-like franchise, the company is significantly underperforming its potential, operating with an 81.8% operating ratio in Q2 2011, compared to 61.3% for its nearest competitor, Canadian National [D06]. This persistent operational lag has left the company’s valuation depressed at approximately 15.1x earnings, a level that fails to account for the substantial self-help opportunity available [D04, D06].

The market has wrongly concluded that CP’s poor performance is a structural byproduct of its network and weather exposure [D03, D05, D06]. We disagree; the efficiency gap is clearly remediable through the implementation of precision railroading [D06]. With a path to reaching an operating ratio in the low 70s, we anticipate normalized earnings potential of C$6.50 to C$7.00 per share [D03, D07]. At current prices, this offers a compelling IRR that captures both margin expansion and a re-rating toward peer multiples [D03, D04].

Our role is to catalyze this change by demanding an overhaul of the board and management to install leadership capable of driving operational discipline [D03, D06]. The primary risk to our thesis is that the existing operational gap is somehow irreducible, though we believe the track record of the broader railroad industry suggests otherwise [D03, D06]. We are initiating a position today with a target of 12% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction that CP represents an undervalued, high-quality compounder whose intrinsic value can be unlocked through active engagement [D03, D06].
